bull_bear.body:
- A skilled workforce guided by experienced, industry-savvy leadership; Executive Chairman associated with the Company as promoter since inception with close to five decades of experience in the specialty paper industry
- Flexibility to adjust product and raw material combinations in response to shifting market demands
- Strong investment in research and development, driving customer-focused innovation; proprietary R&D supports customised product development, tailor-made specifications and faster commercial trials
- Effective cost control and strategic fibre sourcing, enhanced by locational advantages
- Ongoing, meaningful engagement with customers to deliver practical and cost-efficient solutions; reliable, timely delivery with quality commitment and after-sales service
- A broad, adaptable product portfolio designed to meet the diverse requirements of different clients
- Largest specialty paper manufacturing unit at a single location in India, with a well-established pan-India distribution network
- Quality accreditations spanning US FDA, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 22000 and ISO 45001

- Captive 15.4 MW (AC) solar plant supporting long-term energy cost competitiveness
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Structural dependence on purchased fibre, largely imported, with no captive fibre source — The Company states its dependence on purchased fibre, largely imported, remains a structural challenge as it does not have its own fibre sources. The average constitution of raw material is about 27% of sale prices, and any adverse movement in global prices, coupled with geopolitical or transportation imbalances, could disrupt fibre availability and margins. Mitigations cited: maintaining sufficient fibre inventories, adjusting product mix, cost reduction through appropriate fibre quality, and focus on long-term value additions. Market pulp prices ranged between Rs. 47,450 and Rs. 72,900 per MT during the year and wastepaper between Rs. 23,100 and Rs. 32,900 per MT (PROVENANCE: Corporate Overview, profile sibling bundle).
- Energy dependence - minimal cogeneration, reliance on purchased grid power and coal — The Company does not have cogeneration facilities except a small facility of 0.5 MW; at present 27% of its power is drawn from green energy including three wind turbines and one solar plant. Coal prices used by the Company stood at about Rs 11,600 per MT. Renewable expansion (the 15.4 MW AC solar facility at Bhalwani, about 50 km from Solapur) is the stated mitigation.
- Carbon Credit Trading Scheme emission-intensity targets that operations have limited scope to meet — A Gazette notification of 8 October 2025 under the CCTS ('Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules 2025') assigns the Company, based on 2023-24 product output, emission intensity targets of 1.7275 tCO2 equivalent per tonne of product for 2025-26 and 1.6567 for 2026-27. Given manufacturing of specialty papers using imported pulp, purchased grid power and coal as boiler fuel, the scope to meet these targets is stated to be limited; the Company is raising objections to the target-setting methodology versus other paper mills, and views the 15.4 MW solar plant as interim relief.
- Regulatory change on power banking (MERC order) eroding the economics of captive solar — The MERC general order of March 2026 changed banking norms, restricting consumption of self-generated power to solar hours only, cutting the renewable share of annual power requirement from about 38% to 31% with lapse of the remaining power. The matter is in appeal before APTEL, which has stayed the order until judgement; a BESS at Bhalwani is being considered to avoid the lapse. PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, delivered in the profile and strategy_outlook sibling bundles - not in this bundle's text.
- Water security at the Pune plant — Water requirements are met from the Pawna River through an adjacent lifting point. Growing urbanisation around the plant, declining river levels and deteriorating water quality present concerns that could increase operational costs in the future. Compliance with stringent government effluent discharge norms has always been maintained.
- Price competition and commoditisation pressure from commodity paper makers and cheaper imports — Other companies manufacturing commodity papers are competing with some Pudumjee products given the higher realisations they fetch; some competitors have inherent lower cost from location, others produce lower-quality paper at lesser cost. It therefore becomes necessary at times to pass on the benefit of cost reduction to customers without compromising quality or margins - revenue was held flat in FY26 by higher tonnage (1675 MT more) at lower average net sales realisation per MT. PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, profile/strategy_outlook sibling bundles.
- Capacity constraint at the existing site and an unresolved growth-capacity path — The Company operates at about 95% of its installed capacity of 72000 MT per annum, leaving little headroom. Relocation to Mahad remains on hold; the 68,000 MT per annum Mahad facility requires a fresh Environmental Clearance following the Supreme Court judgement in Vanashakti versus Union of India (August 2025), and the AR is internally inconsistent on whether clearance is secured or still being obtained. Existing Pune operations run partly on buildings leased from promoter-group entities AMJ Land Holdings Ltd and 3P Land Holdings Ltd.
- Customer concentration — The segment note discloses that a material share of revenue is derived from a single external customer, attributed to the Paper segment, and reports it separately for both FY26 and FY25 (amounts not reproduced here - they sit in a financial-statement note). PROVENANCE: Note 29 Segment information, delivered under the RELATED-PARTY TRANSACTIONS heading in the profile and governance_entities sibling bundles.
- Unorganised-sector competition in the new paper bags / paper cups vertical — The Hygiene Products Division's newly established vertical supplying paper bags and paper cups has received good response, but the business is dominated by many unorganised players and it may take more time to achieve fair profitability. PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, profile/strategy_outlook sibling bundles.

business.body: The Company specialises in papers tailored for distinct uses, particularly where specific qualities such as resistance to oil and grease are essential, serving the food, pharmaceutical and hygiene industries along with select industrial applications. It operates on a business-to-business model, supplying directly to clients or through a nationwide dealer network while exporting to neighbouring countries and Europe. Its specialty paper machines run at comparatively lower speeds to produce lighter grammage papers, and its Hygiene Products division supplies tissues and related hygiene products to institutional clients such as businesses, hotels, airports and corporate establishments; fibre is met through imported pulp and limited quantities of pre-consumer wastepaper.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Specialty Paper:** Laminated papers engineered for food-grade and pharmaceutical packaging, Baking papers and related specialty grades, Decor papers for furniture laminates and base sheets for melamine tableware, Packaging papers for hygiene products such as napkins, kitchen towels, toilet tissue and baby diapers, Bleached kraft papers for flexible packaging laminates, Premium kraft grades for label release liners, Kraft interleaving for steel and glass applications, Cooling pad papers for household and industrial cooling systems, Fine printing papers for religious texts, dictionaries, pharmaceutical inserts and books, Glassine papers, Low GSM MG papers, Super calendared varieties, crepe tissue and towels, high opacity and low grammage printing papers, Fluorine-free OGR paper (introduced during FY2025-26) - PROVENANCE: stated in the strategy_outlook sibling bundle, not in the profile bundle text, Sustainable barrier papers under accelerated development (moisture/oxygen resistance) - PROVENANCE: strategy_outlook sibling bundle, 80+ specialty paper grades marketed, 450+ customers served - PROVENANCE: strategy_outlook sibling bundle ('BIG NUMBERS')
- **Hygiene Products:** Tissues and related hygiene products for institutional clients, Hygienic hand wash systems and cleaning equipment, Paper Bags and Paper Cups for various applications including the food-grade segment (newly established vertical) - PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, also carried in the strategy_outlook sibling bundle

outlook.body:
- Align market positioning around three strategic pillars - specialisation, sustainability and reliability - to support stronger customer engagement, product relevance and wider participation across specialised paper categories.
- Shift towards higher-value paper solutions (food-grade, fluorine-free OGR and barrier papers) where qualification cycles are longer, customer retention stronger and competitive intensity comparatively lower.
- Respond to price competition, cheaper imports and commoditisation in standard grades by increasing focus on specialised and value-added, application-specific product offerings rather than competing on price.
- Use proprietary in-house R&D for customised product development, tailor-made specifications, faster commercial trials and end-use specific solutions; strengthen coordination between marketing, R&D and manufacturing to accelerate development and commercialisation timelines.
- Deepen customer engagement and market reach through CRM-led lead management and servicing systems, dealer outreach, digital communication, faster product sampling and trial support, and increased engagement with export-focused customers.
- Strengthen procurement resilience through supplier diversification, alternate vendor qualification for critical raw materials and engineering goods, long-term supplier partnerships across pulp, waste paper, chemicals and engineering categories, and integrated procurement/inventory planning.
- Advance sustainability-led procurement: responsible fibre sourcing, traceability-led procurement and supply-chain transparency aligned with evolving global packaging and compliance expectations.
- Going forward, explore localisation of sourcing to the extent possible, strategic partnerships, supply-chain digitisation, sustainability-linked sourcing, cost optimisation without compromising quality, procurement support for innovation, and resilience against geopolitical fragmentation.
- Expand import optimisation - direct imports, High Seas procurement and strategic sourcing - to improve freight planning, pricing visibility and cost competitiveness.
- Continue investing in renewable energy: having commissioned the 15.4 MW captive solar plant, management is actively considering a Battery Energy Storage System at Bhalwani and a further solar plant once regulatory clarity on banking and MERC's BESS regulations emerges.
- Progress the Mahad specialty paper facility of 68,000 MT per annum - Environmental Clearance process underway following the Supreme Court's Vanashakti judgement of August 2025, with the Company in advanced discussion with machinery manufacturers.
- Continue to increase value addition across specialty paper applications and strengthen presence within food-grade and other specialised segments such as Pharma and Hygiene, where customer relationships, product qualification capabilities and technical expertise create relatively higher entry barriers; preserve financial flexibility while progressing expansion in a calibrated manner following receipt of necessary regulatory approvals. PROVENANCE: Chairman/financial-review 'Way forward' text, delivered in the capex_expansion sibling bundle, not in this bundle.
- Company-stated business strategy: continually improve product specifications to align with evolving market requirements; upgrade manufacturing facilities with customised and sustained technologies to maximise asset utilisation; actively identify and leverage market growth opportunities; expand the product portfolio with value-added offerings; emphasise environmental responsibility through initiatives reducing greenhouse gas emissions. PROVENANCE: Corporate Overview 'BUSINESS STRATEGY OF THE COMPANY', delivered in the profile and risks_esg sibling bundles.
- The Company's stated approach is conservative: a conservative Balance Sheet and prudent leverage, with working capital requirements largely financed internally without reliance on short-term bank borrowings except routine letter-of-credit facilities, and the FY2025-26 capital expenditure programme funded substantially through internal accruals with only limited incremental borrowing linked to project execution. Management continues to prioritise liquidity preservation, prudent leverage management and disciplined capital deployment while maintaining preparedness for future expansion opportunities, and intends to preserve financial flexibility while progressing future expansion initiatives in a calibrated manner following receipt of necessary regulatory approvals (PROVENANCE: Chairman's/financial-review chapter, delivered in the capex_expansion sibling bundle). On distribution, the Board recommends a dividend for the year ended 31st March 2026 at the rate of Rs.0.60 per share subject to shareholder approval, with a transfer to General Reserve, and a resolution to declare the dividend is item 3 of the 12th AGM ordinary business (PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, profile sibling bundle; the AGM Notice in this bundle carries the declaration resolution). Shareholders are also being asked, by Special Resolution at the AGM, to permit the Board to invite and accept public deposits within the limits of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014 - the Company had a fixed deposit liability of Rs.798.25 Lakhs as at 31st March 2026 against Rs.808.80 Lakhs a year earlier, with no defaults in repayment of deposits or interest (PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, profile/strategy_outlook sibling bundles). Amounts other than these named policy figures are not reproduced.
- CCTS emission-intensity targets: 1.7275 tCO2 equivalent per tonne of product for 2025-26 and 1.6567 for 2026-27, assigned under the Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules 2025 based on 2023-24 product output.
- Operations up to 31st March 2026 indicate 1.677 tCO2 equivalent per tonne of equivalent product (i.e. against a 1.7275 target for 2025-26).
- For 2026-27, barring unforeseen circumstances, the Company estimates about 1.6208 tCO2 equivalent per tonne of equivalent product against a target of 1.6567.
- 15.4 MW (AC) solar generation facility established at Bhalwani, about 50 kilometers from Solapur, to strengthen sustainability efforts and provide interim relief on emission-intensity targets.
- At present 27% of power is drawn from green energy, including three wind turbines and one solar plant; the Company continues to expand its renewable portfolio with short and long term arrangements aimed at increasing access to green energy.
- FY2025-26 renewable/self-generated energy sourcing: 2647 MVAh wind (2.9% of total power requirement), 21796 MVAh solar (23.84%) and 3558 MVAh self cogeneration (3.89%). PROVENANCE: Annexure-5 Conservation of Energy, capex_expansion sibling bundle.
- Energy-conservation capital investments during the year: hydraulic headbox on two paper machines (improved productivity), an Atmospheric Fluidised Bed Combustion Boiler (reduced coal consumption, enhanced steam productivity) and upgraded Air Circuit Breakers at Motor Control Centers of two paper machines. PROVENANCE: Annexure-5, capex_expansion sibling bundle.
- The solar plant is expected to reduce carbon footprint by about 27000 MT and about 38% of annual power requirement would comprise renewable energy (reduced to 31% under the MERC banking order now stayed by APTEL). PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, profile/strategy_outlook sibling bundles.
- Compliance with stringent effluent discharge norms prescribed by the Government has always been maintained; water is drawn from the Pawna River.
- Environmental responsibility is a stated strategic priority through initiatives aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting a cleaner future.
- Governance/social controls: a Risk Management Policy has been adopted and implemented; a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy is in place and no complaint was received under it during the year.
- An Internal Complaints Committee under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 is constituted, covering the Company and other companies in the Pudumjee Group; no complaints relating to discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment, were received during the year, none pending beyond ninety days and none unresolved as on 31st March 2026.
- The Company is compliant with the statutory provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
- Board evaluation conducted per SEBI master circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/CIR/P/0155 dated 11th November 2024; independent directors met on 31st January 2026; evaluation criteria and familiarisation programme published on the Company website.
- Quality and safety accreditations held: US FDA, ISO 9001, ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), ISO 22000 (Food Safety) and ISO 45001 (Occupational health and safety). PROVENANCE: Corporate Snapshot 'Quality accreditations', profile sibling bundle - back-filled here because no BRSR/ESG chapter was routed into this bundle.
- Sustainability-led procurement: responsible fibre sourcing and traceability-led procurement, strengthened supply-chain transparency and sustainability governance, aligned with evolving global packaging and compliance expectations. PROVENANCE: procurement chapter, strategy_outlook sibling bundle.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY2025-26 was an investment year. The Company states it successfully completed a capex programme of over Rs.110 crores comprising installation of an Atmospheric Fluidised Bed Combustion (AFBC) boiler, modernisation of certain important parts of three of the paper making machines, and setting up of a Solar Power Plant. The Chairman's/financial-review chapter describes the programme as approximately H125 Cr focused on renewable energy integration, operational reliability and manufacturing efficiency, of which approximately H110 Cr was incurred during the year, executed with limited incremental borrowing and funded substantially through internal accruals. The 15.4 MW (AC) solar power plant at Bhalwani, near Solapur (about 50 km from Solapur), was set up and operationalised in December 2025; the Corporate Overview notes the project faced delays from complexities in acquiring land directly from farmers. With it, about 38% of annual power requirement would comprise renewable energy and carbon footprint would fall by about 27000 MT; a MERC general order of March 2026 restricting consumption to solar hours cuts that share to 31%, and the matter is under appeal before APTEL, which has stayed the order. Management is actively considering a Battery Energy Storage System at Bhalwani to avoid lapse of power, and a further Solar Power Plant in due course, once banking-framework clarity and MERC's BESS regulations emerge. Other technology-absorption investments during the year: a new hydraulic headbox on two paper machines, upgradation of the approach flow system on one paper machine, a new QCS system on one paper machine, and upgraded Air Circuit Breakers at the Motor Control Centers of two paper machines. On growth capacity: plans to relocate operations to Mahad, Maharashtra remain on hold; the Corporate Overview says the Company has secured Environmental Clearance subject to conditions for a capacity expansion of approximately 68000 MT at an estimated investment of Rs. 1350 crores, while the Directors' Report says the Company is in the process of obtaining Environmental Clearance for a 68,000 MT per annum specialty paper facility at Mahad, made necessary by the Supreme Court judgement in Vanashakti versus Union of India in August 2025 setting aside the Central Government notification dated 29.1.2025 - the two statements in the same AR are inconsistent on whether the clearance is secured or still being obtained. The Company is in advanced discussion with overseas machinery manufacturers to finalise machine configurations and optimise capital expenditure. Existing operations continue in Pune on freehold land and leased buildings under agreements with AMJ Land Holdings Ltd and 3P Land Holdings Ltd, and the existing site's limitations are cited as the reason expansion at Mahad is under active consideration. The Company operates at about 95% of its installed capacity of 72000 MT per annum (PROVENANCE: MD&A 'Concerns and Threats', delivered in the risks_esg sibling bundle). Management intends to preserve financial flexibility while progressing future expansion initiatives in a calibrated manner following receipt of necessary regulatory approvals. NOTE: the '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE - CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' block in this bundle arrived with its lead-in line only ('Capital expenditure contracted for at the end of the reporting period but not recognised as liability is as follows:') and NO figure, no column dates and a conflicting caption line, so no rupee capital-commitment quantum could be captured.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The specialty paper industry is undergoing a gradual transition towards sustainable, food-safe and application-oriented paper solutions, with customers expecting technical collaboration, dependable execution, faster responsiveness and consistent supply reliability alongside product quality.
- Demand for recyclable, food-compliant and high-performance paper solutions continued to rise in FY2025-26 as packaging companies and industrial customers increasingly explored alternatives to conventional plastic-based materials.
- This transition created opportunities across barrier papers, food-contact applications, flexible packaging solutions and customised technical grades for specialised end-use requirements.
- Some industry segments faced pressure from lower-cost imports, pricing volatility and commoditisation across standard paper categories; manufacturers with stronger product development capabilities, application-specific expertise and customer engagement models are becoming better positioned to participate in higher-value and relatively more stable paper segments.
- Looking ahead, the specialty paper market is expected to see increasing demand for sustainable packaging solutions, specialised paper applications and higher-performan[ce ...] - the routed text truncates mid-word here, so the remainder of the outlook statement is not available.
- Procurement cost pressure: costs across engineering goods and specialised equipment increased on rising prices of copper, aluminium, platinum, silver, graphite and carbon-based products amid supply shortages and rising global demand; imported engineering equipment also became more expensive due to currency volatility, freight inflation and tariff-related pressures.
- Revenue was maintained by larger tonnage of paper by 1675 MT while lowering average net sales realization per MT to pass on the benefit of cost reduction to customers, because commodity paper manufacturers are competing against Pudumjee's higher-realisation products.
- The Hygiene Products Division achieved about 17% improvement in its revenue, catering mainly to institutional customers; the newly established Paper Bags and Paper Cups vertical has received good response but the segment is dominated by unorganised players so fair profitability may take more time.
- Renewable energy integration is expected to support long-term cost competitiveness, operational sustainability and improved energy efficiency across manufacturing operations. PROVENANCE: 'Way forward' text delivered in the capex_expansion sibling bundle.

risks.note: The Company states its dependence on purchased fibre, largely imported, remains a structural challenge as it does not have its own fibre sources. The average constitution of raw material is about 27% of sale prices, and any adverse movement in global prices, coupled with geopolitical or transportation imbalances, could disrupt fibre availability and margins. Mitigations cited: maintaining sufficient fibre inventories, adjusting product mix, cost reduction through appropriate fibre quality, and focus on long-term value additions. Market pulp prices ranged between Rs. 47,450 and Rs. 72,900 per MT during the year and wastepaper between Rs. 23,100 and Rs. 32,900 per MT (PROVENANCE: Corporate Overview, profile sibling bundle).
risks.risk: Structural dependence on purchased fibre, largely imported, with no captive fibre source

risks.note: The Company does not have cogeneration facilities except a small facility of 0.5 MW; at present 27% of its power is drawn from green energy including three wind turbines and one solar plant. Coal prices used by the Company stood at about Rs 11,600 per MT. Renewable expansion (the 15.4 MW AC solar facility at Bhalwani, about 50 km from Solapur) is the stated mitigation.
risks.risk: Energy dependence - minimal cogeneration, reliance on purchased grid power and coal

risks.note: A Gazette notification of 8 October 2025 under the CCTS ('Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules 2025') assigns the Company, based on 2023-24 product output, emission intensity targets of 1.7275 tCO2 equivalent per tonne of product for 2025-26 and 1.6567 for 2026-27. Given manufacturing of specialty papers using imported pulp, purchased grid power and coal as boiler fuel, the scope to meet these targets is stated to be limited; the Company is raising objections to the target-setting methodology versus other paper mills, and views the 15.4 MW solar plant as interim relief.
risks.risk: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme emission-intensity targets that operations have limited scope to meet

risks.note: The MERC general order of March 2026 changed banking norms, restricting consumption of self-generated power to solar hours only, cutting the renewable share of annual power requirement from about 38% to 31% with lapse of the remaining power. The matter is in appeal before APTEL, which has stayed the order until judgement; a BESS at Bhalwani is being considered to avoid the lapse. PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, delivered in the profile and strategy_outlook sibling bundles - not in this bundle's text.
risks.risk: Regulatory change on power banking (MERC order) eroding the economics of captive solar

risks.note: Water requirements are met from the Pawna River through an adjacent lifting point. Growing urbanisation around the plant, declining river levels and deteriorating water quality present concerns that could increase operational costs in the future. Compliance with stringent government effluent discharge norms has always been maintained.
risks.risk: Water security at the Pune plant

risks.note: Other companies manufacturing commodity papers are competing with some Pudumjee products given the higher realisations they fetch; some competitors have inherent lower cost from location, others produce lower-quality paper at lesser cost. It therefore becomes necessary at times to pass on the benefit of cost reduction to customers without compromising quality or margins - revenue was held flat in FY26 by higher tonnage (1675 MT more) at lower average net sales realisation per MT. PROVENANCE: Directors' Report, profile/strategy_outlook sibling bundles.
risks.risk: Price competition and commoditisation pressure from commodity paper makers and cheaper imports

risks.note: The Company operates at about 95% of its installed capacity of 72000 MT per annum, leaving little headroom. Relocation to Mahad remains on hold; the 68,000 MT per annum Mahad facility requires a fresh Environmental Clearance following the Supreme Court judgement in Vanashakti versus Union of India (August 2025), and the AR is internally inconsistent on whether clearance is secured or still being obtained. Existing Pune operations run partly on buildings leased from promoter-group entities AMJ Land Holdings Ltd and 3P Land Holdings Ltd.
risks.risk: Capacity constraint at the existing site and an unresolved growth-capacity path
